reading: Every round this line has been judged as the best-set page in its field, and the judges have mostly stopped arguing about that. They love the figure-left/rows-right rack, the one rule held on every page (every list in time hangs from a rail with one lit NOW, and amber, sky and bone each keep one job), the round tubes on Plans and Status (soul calls them "the most beautiful new tubes on the panel"), the bone condensed heads with one lit word, the weekday/mono-date split on the rails, the Late 3 tab, the plain-sentence fix on Status and the 13-14px text floor. System gave it 8.5 and usability 8.0. Four things keep pulling it down, and every lens names at least one of them. (1) Figures that repeat their list. Home's Fig. 1 graph-paper date grid is "decoration posing as data" (skeptic, twice). The "Next in 2 days" tube says what rail stop 1 says (feedback, interaction, usability, skeptic). To do's counter and Chat's sequence panel duplicate their lists (interaction). (2) Figures that are grey and drawn rather than lit, on graph paper that edges toward costume (feedback, soul, skeptic). (3) The greeting: a big sans headline with a bright green word "reads like a modern landing page rather than a lit word on a screen" (soul), with no lit board or pool behind it (feedback). (4) The figure column takes width on pages where it earns nothing (system, interaction, usability), and Plans keeps its 90px gap and its broken month NOW trace. To win, it must keep the rail-and-NOW grammar and the typesetting exactly, keep a figure only where it shows something the list cannot, and light the figures that stay. The other camp has solved each of these. Backlit Plate draws time as a lit slot trace. Quote Board puts the page's count in the head. Desk Terminal ends every page in a Ready foot. Dessau lights the question from below. Each can be rebuilt in bone, blueprint and phosphor so it reads native to the manual.

briefs.name: Lit Manual, Slotted
briefs.hypothesis: The carried design already holds the line's best scores for system, type and usability. What it loses on is figures that repeat their rows, figures drawn in grey on graph paper, a greeting that reads as a SaaS hero, and a figure column that takes width on every page. This cross keeps the rail and its one lit NOW untouched. It replaces each figure that repeats with one that shows what the list cannot: the next four weeks with free weekends, lit on glass; the page's count in its head; the machine's state in its colophon. It lights every figure that stays, gives the greeting the original page's pool of light from below, and folds the figure column away wherever no figure earns it. Each judge's top complaint is answered by a feature another lens already scored at 8 or above elsewhere. The manual should read as well set as before and as lit as the original tube where the machine is live, which is the owner's latest ask.
briefs.brief:
Start from the parent's files: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/cross/x14a-a/variants/t3-figure-refine/ (sheet.css, templates/, static/) and palettes/t3-figure-refine.json. Keep every token, both faces (Plex Sans Condensed heads, Plex Sans text, Plex Mono figures, VT323 only on glass), the bone #e8e2d0 heads, the blueprint #9fb4d6 links and drawing ink #6f88b3, amber only for late, and the rail grammar (.railed, now_rule(), rail_mark(), rail_day(), the --rail-x line, one lit NOW per list).

SYSTEM RULES, written into the top of sheet.css and docs as the standard:
(a) A figure column (--fig-w) appears only on pages whose figure shows something the rows do not: Status (the wiring), To do (deadlines against NOW) and Plans (the countdown ring). Everywhere else the page is one column at a 46rem measure for prose and full width for lists, and the rail's own line at --rail-x is the figure.
(b) No graph paper. Set --grid-fine and --grid-bold to transparent and remove every background-image grid on .fig and the plates. A figure sits on --sheet #0e1513 with a 1px --sheet-edge and 3px corners (new token --r-plate: 3px; chips and keys get --r-chip: 3px instead of square corners), and the corner tick marks go.
(c) What is live in a figure is lit. Ports, stops and counters that mean 'on' or 'next' are lamps: white-hot core var(--lit-core) as a radial gradient, a 5px bloom and a 14px halo (E20/E21 of phosphor_kit.md), breathing over 3.2s. Lit wires and the NOW line are the screen at full strength with var(--lit-mark). Everything else in a figure is drawing ink, matte.
(d) Captions: drop the 'Fig. n' prefix where the caption only labels (Coming up, Ideas, Chat). Keep 'Fig.' only on the three drawn figures. Set 'FIG.', 'NOW' and eyebrows in true small caps (font-variant-caps: all-small-caps; letter-spacing .06em), with a caption floor at --t-cap: 400 0.875rem/20px var(--f-text).
(e) One NOW label everywhere: small caps, Plex Mono 600 0.8125rem, #6dff9c with E1's two-layer halo, at the same height relative to its line on Home's Coming up, Home's To do and the To do page.

HOME (templates/home.html, the .welcome plate and the .day plate):
1. The title: proposed 'Give Vera something to *plan*.', in --t-question (52px Plex Sans Condensed 600, bone). 'plan' is #6dff9c with E1's halo plus a hot core (text-shadow: 0 0 1px var(--lit-core), 0 0 4px rgb(109 255 156/.9), 0 0 18px rgb(109 255 156/.45)), and the full stop is inside the lit run. Behind it, .welcome::before lays the original page's pool lit from below (E7): a radial 16% phosphor core centred under 'plan' where the box begins, plus a 10% pool at the box's lower left, seen through 1px-in-4px scanlines masked by the same radial, so the light rises round the word and spills onto the box's top edge. Scanlines stay inside the mask only.
2. The tube at the right of the welcome becomes 'The next four weeks', a slot window (graft A below) and no longer a radar plus countdown. Inside the glass, line 1 is the VT323 bright 'Next in 2 days' with the block cursor. Under it is a 28-day slot trace: NOW a breathing lamp at the left edge, a numbered pulse for each coming plan whose numeral is the same number as its rail stop (1-4) so no legend is needed, the next pulse lit with the hot core and the rest at dim strength, and weekends drawn as sage bands at 8% (--slot-weekend: rgb(134 217 166/.08)). A weekend with no plan reads as a clear band, and the glass foot says it in words ('weekend of 10 Oct free'). This is what the list cannot show. The plan's name is not printed on desktop (rail row 1 says it). On the phone, the name prints under 'Next in 2 days'. The glass keeps E13/E14 (bloom, 0.35px blur, scanlines, corner falloff) and the case and power light (E12). The radar leaves Home and lives on Ideas.
3. Coming up drops Fig. 1, the date grid, entirely. Its rows span the plate. The rail at --rail-x carries the numbered stops and the weekday/mono-date split, and NOW is lit at the top. Coming up and To do sit side by side as now, with To do's NOW tick in the same small-caps label as Coming up's.
4. The jump row (nav.jump) shows on desktop too, under the starters, as three keys with a tabular figure over a small-caps label ('3 / MORE PLANS', '4 / TO DO', '3 / LATE' in amber words, never an amber outline). The figure is Plex Sans Condensed 600 1.5rem; on the phone it is the same keys at full width.
5. The lower half gets the rail-and-row treatment instead of going flat. Finish setting up keeps its numbered rings on a blueprint line, ending in the hollow ring and 'Then you're ready.' (no amber card or outline). The kids' wishes collapse to one line when nothing is open ('Maya, Theo · nothing open · All →'). Lately added keeps its two columns, but the kind square becomes a 6px lamp-less ink square in the kind colour.

TO DO (templates/tasks.html): the head row is the Quote Board figure head (graft B): 'Things to do' then '4' in the todo wheat #e5d183, stacked 'OPEN' in small caps over '▸ 3 late' in amber, linking to the Late tab. Add something to do stays as the green primary at the right. Fig. 1, the person counter, is removed. Fig. 2, each task at its deadline against NOW, stays as the one figure, narrowed to an 11rem rail-only gutter: date labels in mono, late stops as small amber lamps with a halo, and the NOW lamp lit with a line that crosses the list. The list gains the width back. The Show keys (Open, Late 3, Done, Cancelled, All) keep their place under the head.

PLANS (plans_month.html, plans.html): the head row carries '4 plans' as its figure. The round countdown gauge stays in the figure column at 13rem and names the plan inside its caption ('Next: Oaks Park roller rink, Sun 4 Oct 13:00'), so the separate Next line goes and the ~90px gap closes: the month grid starts directly under the head and its List/Month keys. The left-hand week rail is cut (usability), because the month itself carries time. Today's cell is outlined in phosphor, and a dim afterglow trace (rgb(109 255 156/.25), 1px) runs from the grid's left edge along today's week row into today's outline, so the NOW is unbroken. Week ranges, where shown in the list view, are in Plex Mono tabular.

STATUS (status.html): the head figure is '3 of 4' answering, in bone, stacked 'ANSWERING' / '1 key set'. The spend gauge stays at top right with its bloom raised one step (outer spill 0 0 60px -10px at .45). Fig. 1, the wiring, stays and is lit: the ports in use are lamps with white-hot cores, the wire from the key in use to the model runs at full screen glow, and the off ports are pewter rings (2px #8794a2). The figure fills the column at 16.5rem with no graph paper. Row states ('Working', 'Off', 'Needs a look') are set in the lamp's own dim ink beside its name, not in a separate right-aligned column.

IDEAS (ideas.html): no figure column. The head row is 'Ideas' with '12' (the ideas violet #ab89d2 is held to the figure only) over 'IDEAS', then Add an idea. Under the lede, a 12rem radar tube (E17, the same case as the Plans and Status tubes) sits beside the Nearest and Furthest lines. 'Show one kind' becomes one row of latched kind keys with tabular counts above the list (Every kind 12 · Activity 2 · …), and the list takes the full width.

CHAT (chat.html): the separate sequence-diagram panel goes. The thread runs one column at 46rem, with the family's lines on the right as now. The sequence lives in the thread's own left gutter: a 1px drawing-ink lane at --rail-x with a short arrow stub level with each line, pointing in for the family and out for Vera, and the newest line's stub lit at full glow with a lamp at its head. The date divider stays mono.

SETTINGS, FORM AND FAMILY: the figure column collapses (rule a). Setup stays a numbered rail. Section cards keep their state words and get the row afterglow.

EVERY PAGE: the footer's left column (already 336px, under the FamilyDB mark) becomes the manual's colophon, the machine's status foot (graft C): lamp, 'Ready', 'OpenAI · gpt-6-luna' and '$2.00 a day' in Plex Mono tabular, and 'Status →'. On Status it shows '$0.00 of $2.00 today' and is not a link. A kid sees only the lamp and its word. Every row (plan-row, task-line, idea rows, status rows, settings cards) gets the visible row afterglow (graft E) on :hover and :focus-within.

PHONE: every figure folds below its list into a <details> whose summary is its one-line caption, in the Tab order and 44px tall. Home's slot tube sits after the box at 5.5rem tall. The tab bar keeps its icons.
briefs.borrows:
Own judges' fixes, most cited first:
- Home Fig. 1 repeats the list: remove it, and make the figure show what the list cannot, such as free weekends. Asked by skeptic (t3 and landing), interaction (t3, landing), style (landing), feedback (t3).
- Duplicate 'Next in 2 days' tube beside rail stop 1: merge them into one countdown-plus-slot tube that names the plan only on the phone. Asked by feedback, interaction, usability, skeptic (t3) and style (t3).
- Figures grey and drawn on graph paper: light them as lamps and wires, and drop the grids. Asked by feedback (landing), soul (t3 counters as lamps, landing 'drop the faint blueprint grid'), skeptic (landing 'drop graph-paper backgrounds, round the chips slightly').
- Greeting reads as a SaaS hero: E1 halo with a hot core and a lit pool behind it. Asked by soul (landing) and feedback (landing 'a lit board behind the greeting').
- Figure column only where it earns it; Ideas' radar to the head; give lists the width. Asked by system (landing), interaction (t3, landing), usability (t3 220px gutter).
- Chat's sequence panel duplicates the thread: fold it into the gutter. Asked by interaction (t3, landing), feedback (t3), skeptic (landing).
- Plans: close the 90px gap, carry the month NOW through, make the gauge name the plan, cut the left week rail. Asked by feedback, style, system and skeptic (t3), soul (t3) and usability (landing).
- One NOW label at one height, and small caps for NOW, FIG. and eyebrows. Asked by system, type and skeptic (t3).
- Drop 'Fig.' where self-evident, with a caption floor at 0.8rem or more. Asked by style and system (landing), type (landing).
- Home's lower half goes flat: rail-and-row treatment. Asked by system (landing).
- Phone: figures folded below their lists, tabular large numerals on the counters, and summary keys on desktop. Asked by usability, type and interaction (landing).
- Status words in the lamp's dim ink. Asked by system (t3).

briefs.avoids:
The duplicate-figure charge: the date grid, the separate Next tube text, To do's counter and Chat's sequence panel are each removed or merged, and every remaining figure shows something its rows do not (free weekends, deadlines against now, the wiring). The 'cold engineering costume' charge: graph paper goes, chips get 3px corners, and 'Fig.' stays only on drawn figures. The 'SaaS hero' charge: the lit word gets E1 plus a hot core and the original pool of light from below, through scanlines. The 'grey figures' charge: live marks become lamps and wires at full glow. The 'figure column takes width' charge: the column is kept only on Status, To do and Plans, and Ideas, Chat, Home's Coming up and Settings get the full measure. Plans' 90px gap and broken NOW trace are fixed. The NOW labels are unified. The flat lower half of Home is railed. Across rounds it also avoids what sank others: amber appears only as words, a row edge or a small lamp, never as outlines or cards; there are no inverted-green chips; the rails are lit only from now to next; no starters scroll sideways on the phone; and no clock time is invented for an untimed task.

What it gives up to make room: Home's radar (it moves to Ideas), Home's Fig. 1 date grid, the graph-paper texture that was part of the manual look, Chat's separate sequence figure, To do's person counter, Plans' left-hand week rail, Status's '3 of 4 / 1 of 4' stat row (now the head figure), and 'Fig.' numbering on captions that only label.
briefs.title: Give Vera something to *plan*. This title has not been tried. It keeps everything that made the lineage's 'Tell Vera what to plan.' win all eight notes in tour heat b. It is an imperative that names who hears you, the lit four-letter job word sits at the line's end where the eye stops, and the full stop belongs to the lit run. It answers that title's one cost, 'slightly more instructional than inviting', in two ways. 'Give' makes the box a hand-over to her rather than an order. 'Something' takes in every kind of thing FamilyDB keeps (a weekend plan, an idea for someday, a reminder, a wish), so it neither narrows the job to 'next' nor presumes a plan exists the way 'our plan' did. Unlike 'Anything to plan?', it cannot be answered 'no'. It holds two lines on a phone ('Give Vera something / to plan.') at the 52px step, with the halo on four letters only.
